Primary responsibilities Machinist
•     Operate machine tools such as lathes, milling machines,
•     Manufacture rods, glands, pistons, barrels, bases, fittings, bushes
•     Review specifications for a job.
•     Calculate where to cut or bore.

•     Detect problems by listening for specific sounds.

•     Monitor the accuracy of cuts.
•     Replace dull cutting tools.
•     Check accuracy of work against specifications.
•     Ability to use precision tools (eg. Micrometers internal & external)

Primary responsibilities Fitter

•     Seal assembly
•     Then test cylinder, make sure has no leaks, by- pass pressure test, close it up, plug and press in the bushes
•     Record the testing
•     ID cylinder with job number
•     Completed cylinder for spraying
•     Torque nuts and bolts to right specifications
•     Press the bushes

Qualifications/Knowledge/Skills/Experience
 
•     Certificate Ill in Engineering - Mechanical Trade (Fitter & Machinist)
•     Good mechanical aptitude.
•     Excellent reading comprehension
•     Physical Stamina

if you have the required qualifications and experience and are looking to advance your career with a respected engineering business.

Job description:

Why join us at Alliance?

- We value your time - great company culture where flexibility and work-life balance are valued
- Grow your skills and expertise - work for a company that supports your professional development
- Wellbeing allowance - we care about your wellbeing
- Social events - company social events
- Friendly workplace - enjoy working in a friendly, professional environment

About us:

Alliance Geotechnical is an established and highly regarded geotechnical and environmental engineering consultancy with a proven track record in providing engineering and testing services on large scale civil infrastructure projects. Established in 2003, we have over 150 employees based in our office and materials testing laboratory in Seven Hills, NSW. Alliance Geotechnical offers a great working culture and competitive remuneration package.

To learn more about Alliance and what we can offer you, please go to https://allgeo.com.au/about/#benefits.

The opportunity

We are looking for a highly driven Geotechnical Engineer to join our established Sydney Geotechnical Engineering team of approx. 45 people. You’ll be involved in investigations, analysis and construction support, working alongside experienced engineers and scientists in a genuinely supportive, collaborative environment. Expect a combination of field, lab and office work with some travel to regional NSW sites when projects require it.

Key responsibilities

- Fieldwork planning including subcontractor engagement and preparation of documentation contributing to safe, efficient site operations.
- Supervision of test pit excavation and borehole drilling operations, soil/rock logging to AS 1726, sampling, in-situ testing and on-site 
coordination.
- Scheduling of laboratory testing, collation and interpretation of results with guidance and review.
- Preparation of factual logs, figures and draft report sections, participation in quality reviews to ensure high technical standards.
- Assistance with geotechnical analysis and provision of practical inputs for foundations, retaining structures, slopes, pavements and earthworks.
- Clear communication with internal teams and clients, seeking support and feedback as necessary.

You will experience engineering projects from concept through to construction—not just desktop work—as we support your development into a well-rounded geotechnical engineer or engineering geologist.

About you

- Tertiary qualification in Civil/Geotechnical Engineering or Engineering Geology.
- Driver’s licence and appetite for fieldwork (metro and occasional regional NSW).
- Clear written and verbal communication with strong time-management and organisational skills.
- Solid Microsoft Office skills and a willingness to learn industry software and data systems.
- Familiarity with Australian Standards (e.g., AS 1726) and a practical, safety-first mindset.

What we offer

- Flexible, people-first culture that respects work–life balance.
- Structured graduate development program and mentorship with clear feedback and on-the-job coaching (you will always know what “good” looks like, and why).
- Exposure to a wide range of projects ranging from small residential to major city-shaping infrastructure.
- Wellbeing allowance, regular social events, and a friendly, professional team.
- Real progression pathways with opportunity to grow into providing design inputs, construction phase services, specialist assessments and more.

Salary Range: $79,423 - $83,000

How to apply

Please send your resume, cover letter and a copy of your degree.

result.description:
Quality Assurance Officer position available in all states NSW, Qld, Vic, & WA

At NEPEAN™ we are proud to be Australia’s leading privately owned engineering, mining services and industrial manufacturing organisation. We have unique capabilities to deliver high value, innovative and sustainable solutions for the world’s leading mining, construction, and transport companies. Over the last 40 years, hard work, technical credibility, and a willingness to tackle very difficult projects have earned NEPEAN an enviable reputation. Today our organisation employs over 1400 people across six continents and distributes products to more than 65 countries

We service our customers through multiple businesses in our portfolio: NEPEAN Building and Infrastructure (Galserv, Galintel, Weldlok), NEPEAN Engineering and Innovation, NEPEAN Power, Mining (NEPEAN Longwall), PROK, NEPEAN Conveyors, NEPEAN Transport, Gurtec, Roxon, and NEPEAN Belting Mackay.

The Role
As QA Officer, you are responsible for ensuring that all products and services consistently meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This involves performing tests, identifying defects, documentation, and assisting in process improvements.

Your Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Conduct routine quality assurance inspections and testing of materials, components to ensure compliance with Australian Standards and ISO 9001 quality requirements
Develop and implement quality control plans (QCP) and inspection test plans (ITP) for mechanical systems, welding, and assembly operations
Maintain, review, and update quality documentation, including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), batch records, and, in some cases, product specifications
Monitor and ensure product quality throughout the production process, following ISO 9001 and industry-specific standards
Investigate product quality issues, identify root causes, and prepare reports on non-conforming materials or processes
Prepare detailed quality documentation including test reports, inspection records, and final dossiers for client handover
Collaborate with design, production, and maintenance teams to resolve quality issues and ensure continuous improvement of products
Ensure testing equipment is properly maintained, calibrated, and used according to protocols
Ensure compliance with Work Health and Safety (WHS) requirements in all QA-related activities
Coordinate third-party inspections and liaise with suppliers to verify conformance of mechanical parts and supplied materials, ensuring they meet company standards
Document quality assurance activities and create audit reports.

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Previous work experience in quality assurance or a similar field.
Working knowledge of tools, methods, and concepts of quality assurance.
Solid knowledge of relevant regulatory standards.
Good communication skills, both verbal and written.
Excellent data collection and analysis skills
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills, with high attention to detail.

If you believe you have the right skills, experience and passion for succeeding in this role, please submit your cover letter and resume for consideration.

NEPEAN believes in diversity and is committed to providing Equal Employment opportunities for all applicants. We welcome applicants from all walks of life which also included various socio-economic, cultural, LGBTIQ, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.

Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Steamatic is Australia’s longest established and largest restoration Company with over 35 locations throughout Australia and growing each year. We have available work Nationwide in Metropolitan and Regional areas.

We are now looking to recruit an experienced and qualified IT Support Technician to join our dedicated service team working in various locations throughout Australia.

The Role
We are looking for technically skilled candidate with good problem-solving ability for the position of IT Support Technician. The duties include being a reference point for all IT related queries at the user level, responding to user needs in a timely manner and ensuring the optimal running of all systems, among other technical duties.

The role includes but is not limited to the following duties:
Installing and configuring hardware and software components to ensure usability
Diagnosing, troubleshooting, and resolving connectivity, hardware, and software issues
Performing tests and evaluations of new software and hardware
Scheduling and conducting quality audit inspections, and analysing and reviewing systems, data and documentation
Identifying variations and potential high-risk areas in securing adherence to standards and procedures
Recommending corrective action plans and improvements in the resolution of non- compliance with standards detected through monitoring and auditing of processes and procedures
Communicating, educating, and liaising with users and management to ensure awareness and adherence to standards, procedures and quality control issues and activities
Assisting in troubleshooting, diagnosing, testing and resolving system problems and issues
Developing, conducting, and offering technical guidance and training in application software and operational procedures
Analysing, evaluating, and diagnosing technical problems and issues such as installation, maintenance, repair, upgrade and configuration and troubleshooting of desktops, software, hardware, printers, Internet, email, databases, operating systems and security systems
Testing, identifying and diagnosing functionality errors and faults in systems, and programming code within established testing protocols, guidelines and quality standards to ensure systems perform to specification
Performing organisational systems architecture reviews and assessments, and recommending current and future hardware and software strategies and directions
Creating and reviewing technical documentation such as procedural, instructional and operational guides and manuals, technical reports and specifications and maintenance inventory systems
Using project management methodologies, principles, and techniques to develop project plans and to cost, resource and manage projects
Test plans, which ensure acceptable quality and integrity of the system
Creating user and training documentation, and conducting formal training classes
Establishing good relationships with all departments and colleagues
Working with users to formulate and document business requirement
Investigating, and analysing business processes, procedures and work practices

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Previous work experience in the same field
3+ years of experience in computer networks and systems maintenance
Proficiency in computer systems, software installation, database programming, and cybersecurity basics
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Good interpersonal skills
Strong problem-solving, and time management skills
Attention to detail
Self-motivated and eager to learn and grow within the organisation

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

About us

An excellent opportunity exists for someone friendly, reliable, efficient and self-motivated to join our ever growing Eye Clinic in Midland to assist with reception and administrative duties, along with some patient pre-testing.

This is a full time position, 5 days a week (Monday to Friday). With multiple doctors covering different ophthalmic sub-specialties, we are a comprehensive provider of eye care and surgery in the local area, servicing both local and regional patients.

Our practice continues to grow with the recent addition of another ophthalmologist to our team, and we are expanding our support staff to ensure we continue to provide exceptional care and service to our patients. This is an opportunity to join a friendly and dynamic team in a busy and progressive practice.

About you

Discretion, empathy and professionalism are of utmost importance to you. You thrive in high pressure, busy environments and are able to problem solve and think on the spot when required. You take pride in being a comforting smiling face for our patients to see and will go above and beyond to make their experience a pleasant and memorable one.

Qualifications & experience

- Previous relevant medical reception, administrative and/or patient testing experience highly regarded

- Ability to cope with high volume patient flow and to prioritize daily schedules to maintain a smooth workflow is a must

- Team focused mindset with the willingness to support clinicians and colleagues-

- High attention to detail and multi-tasking is essential

- Able to show compassion with emotional and intelligent patient interaction

- Resilient and adaptable

- Seamless communication with all clinicians, staff members and management

- Proven ability to use initiative and problem solve issues that may arise

Tasks & responsibilities

- Administrative duties including but not limited to; reception, answering and managing phone enquiries and emails, updating and maintaining accurate patient records, responding to and dealing with patient referrals, end of day banking

- Scheduling a variety of appointments, including surgery bookings requiring high accuracy

- Providing exceptional customer service to patients and other third parties; face-to-face, over the phone and via electronic communication

- Ability to work collaboratively in a team orientated environment

- Perform patient testing including but not limited to; visual acuity, visual field tests, biometry, IOPs, OCT scans and photos as required. Training will be provided for this

Requirements

Applicants must have full, unrestricted working rights in Australia (Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident, or valid visa holder with full work rights)

Information

Easy access via public transport

Career progression opportunities and ongoing professional development

Rostered work days required: Monday to Friday, with variable start and finish times ranging from 8am to 6.30pm, so flexibility is essential

Salary: $55,328 – $69,160 per annum plus superannuation, depending on experience

Please include a cover letter addressed to Vicky listing your qualifications and relevant experience with your application.

Applications without cover letters or AI generated will not be considered. References must be provided.
